messages:
anya: Quick Q — clarifying per-route throttle headers for the quota migration. What should clients expect on 429s? specifically: burst buckets vs overall quotas.
jamal: We return 429 with X-RateLimit-Limit / X-RateLimit-Remaining / X-RateLimit-Reset for token-level quotas. For per-route burst we had discussed a separate X-Route-Burst header. Is that still the plan?
sophia: I thought we were leaning toward a single bucket id header (so clients can group) — the design doc mentioned X-Quota-Bucket as canonical.
mike: FYI, staging currently returns headers like:
```
X-Quota-Bucket: write-heavy-1
Retry-After: 30
Content-Type: application/json
```
and a body: {"error":"rate_limited","scope":"route"}
anya: :thumbsup: Can we standardize on RFC-style names plus a small set of extras? Clients and 3rd-party libs expect `X-RateLimit-*` most of the time.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rolled out quota-header feature to staging (sha: abc123) — no prod rollout yet.
jamal: Proposal: keep X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset for account/global quotas. Add X-RateLimit-Scope: route|global and X-RateLimit-Bucket for bucket id (string). Continue to include Retry-After. Body may include {"retry_in": <secs>} for convenience.
sophia: SGTM. Also we should state behavior: if scope=route and bucket indicates burst, Retry-After should reflect the bucket refill, not the global account window.
mike: I'll open a small PR to rename X-Route-Burst -> X-RateLimit-Bucket, add X-RateLimit-Scope, and document the semantics (PR #3421). Tests on staging already include body.retry_in.
anya: Thanks — can reviewers @jamal @sophia take a look? Need this aligned before quota cutover next week.
jamal: :eyes: will review today.
sophia: I'll check the tests and add a backward-compat note — keep old X-Quota-Bucket / X-Route-Burst as aliases for 30 days.
mike: Done — added alias headers, migration note in docs, and set deprecation window to 30 days. Pushing to staging now; will follow up if any regressions.
anya: Appreciate it — closing this thread unless someone sees an issue.
